Powerless: Eskom

By: Anina Peens | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
As the lights went out again this week across South Africa, we sit down with Eskom's chief in charge to get answers about the utility's plan to curb power cuts.

Unique Selling Point:
a Week before the election, South Africa was left in the dark, again after Eskom announced stage 4 load shedding for the week. We take a look at the reasons why the lights keep going out.

Summary:
After a week of load shedding, we take a look at the affects on the economy. It is said that stage 4 costs the South African economy between 18 and 24 million Rand a day. How did we get here? has Eskom become more of a liability than a lifeline? We sit down with the man at the helm, Andre de Ruyter.


Further information:
Eskom was once considered one of the top power utilities in the world. Today, its name is synonymous with loadshedding, throttling the South African economy. For years, the lifeblood of the country, the power stations, were neglected. Since Andre de Ruyter took over the reins of the embattled state-owned enterprise in 2020, many senior officials are being held accountable for maladministration, corruption and money laundering. But what is being done about the power stations?

Expert:
Mr. Andre De Ruyter CEO
Mr. Chris Yelland Energy Expert
Mr. Mike Schussler Economist

Script:


POWERLESS

Run in: 3” visuals

LINK This week, South Africa lost a third of its power capacity due to Eskom’s power cuts. As if its debt and bailouts are not already overburdening the slow growing economy, power cuts set us back another 24 million Rand an hour. Eskom has become a liability for the economy, instead of a lifeline. And yet, the utility is stuck in the same rut, for 14 years now. And it does not seem that anything is changing.

CUT TO BLACK FOR 3…. AS IT THE POWER OUTAGE CUT HER OFF. THEN ROLL GRAPHIC ON BLACK

GRAPHIC
(SCROLL) Eskom would like to apologise for the inconvenience caused by the implementation of loadshedding, and requests the public to reduce the usage of electricity in order to help us through the constraints.
LINK
MASA
LINK
There it is… Eskom again, asking South Africans to help it out of a crisis IT created. If ESKOM ISNT asking us to reduce THE USE OF electricity we are paying for, IT takes our tax money to bail out THE STATE-OWNED COMPANY. And why IS ESKOM in debt? Because of years and years of mismanagement and deeply rooted corruption by the very people who were supposed to protect arguably the most important utility government has under its control. Yet, Eskom seems to be dishing out the same excuses every time the lights trip.
VO
Economist Mike Schussler says, power cuts are not only costing the economy in hard Rands, it actually has a direct effect on job creation. =30”
VO
One of the FREQUENTLY-CITED reasons IS that Eskom needs more generation capacity. It always seems to need more of this or more of that - coal here, a bail-out there.. but THOSE AT THE HELM FAILED TO maintain a utility that was considered the best in the world as recently as 2001. It is like driving an old car for years, hard, to the ground, and only ever filling up the petrol tank, but never checking the engine.
LINK
Any motorist will tell you that whether your car is old or new, it definitely needs to be well maintained. Especially if it is this old to avoid such things…all I can smell is rubber. Now had this vehicle been maintained consistently, it would obviously be in a far better condition. But like the owner of this vehicle clearly ignored all the red flags, the smoke coming out of the bonnet, the smell, the sounds, the flashing engine lights reminding the owner to service it, and what did they do? They carried on driving. Now imagine, this car was a power station.
VO
And for how long have the red lights being flashing at our power stations? The reason we saw extended power outages this week was because problems occurred at 5 power stations. Eskom only has 15 coal fired power stations. This means, there were issues at a third of the country’s power stations. South Africans were fed up and many took to social media to share their frustration.
VO
Even the ANC – ON THE EVE OF A LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTION THAT HAS BEEN ALL ABOUT POOR SERVICE DELIVERY – was pushing Eskom to explain its renewed blackout schedule. (instead of hinting, let’s just call it what it is)
SUPER@ JESSE DUARTE: ACTING ANC SECRETARY GENERAL
“We’re demanding an answer, we want to know what is going on inside Eskom.”

VO
MORE ELECTIONEERING RHETORIC OR NOT, South Africans want to know what Eskom is doing to save the economy from collapse.

SUPER@ JESSE DUARTE: ANC SECRETARY GENERAL
You can’t put out a statement like that and not give us a reason why… so we need a clear answer from Meneer De Ruyter and the minister

VO
Not realising just how significant the issue would become, we asked Eskom CEO, Andre de Ruyter, about the power cuts in an interview late last week. We were putting together a story on the utility’s power stations and coal procurement, but this week’s blackouts forced a change of plan.
SUPER@ANDRÈ DE RUYTER: CEO, ESKOM
“Loadshedding is going to remain a risk. It is something that we try our level best to avoid.

VO
When he took office almost two years ago, many were hoping De Ruyter would ensure the lights stayed on and that Eskom would start emerging from its deep financial hole. De Ruyted has been visibly focussed on exposing corruption at the utility, but the blackouts remain.
SUPER@ANDRÈ DE RUYTER: CEO, ESKOM
It is very clear that the networks that were created during the state capture years are still very much active and very much alive and the notion that state capture ended when the Gupta brothers’ plane departed Lanseria is not true, it is still carrying on and it is still an ongoing matter.

MASA: But you are the turnaround plan, how is it still going on under your watch?

ADR: That is exactly, when you look at the 42 thousand employees that we’ve got and we look at the patronage networks that exist, it is impossible for an individual no matter how good, to fix Eskom by myself and that is why I always say I can’t fix Eskom but we can fix Eskom.

MASA: Lets talk about the maintenance of power stations. It is public knowledge that it has been declining over the last ten years. From your time here, have you noticed that Eskom bosses have in the past maybe turned a blind eye?

ADR: The focus was not on the basics of the business in terms of maintaining plants ensuring that money was well spent, that proper procurement practices were followed, that information systems were adequately maintained and implemented in order to exercise control over the 100 and thirty odd billion Rand that Eskom spends annually.

MASA: So, what are you doing to ensure that we don’t have the past mistakes of power stations that are not properly maintained? Can you confidently say that today, these power stations are being well maintained? And I doubt you can because we are experiencing loadshedding?

ADR: We are not where we need to be. Systemic neglect was quite evident across all of the Eskom Power stations and also at our transmission and distribution sites with some exceptions. So, we have launched an operations excellence initiative to drive these improved practices but bear in mind that recovering from neglected maintenance is a very tough job to do.

LINK

While a lack of maintenance of the stations is one thing, the coal that is fed into the burners poses another great challenge for the embattled utility. Coal is like the blood that feeds the heart. But in Eskom’s case, not all the blood is clean, creating issues for the heart and preventing it from functioning as it should.

VO
Eskom does not have full control over the procurement of coal. Sometimes rocks, rubble and other materials are fed into the burners but sold for the same price as a load of coal.
Energy expert, Chris Yelland says, 80% of South Africa’s electricity generation depends on coal and it is a big business.

SUPER@ CHRIS YELLAND: ENERGY EXPERT
“Eskom, at one point was supplied largely by the coal majors. Now the coal majors generally built the coal mines right next to the power station and there was this relationship between Eskom and the coal majors and that is what delivered the cheapest coal at a consistent quality to Eskom”

VO
But policy changes around 2003 resulted in Eskom buying coal from a variety of emerging mining companies and thus lost control over coal procurement.

but with the changes in South Africa, there was and I believe it was the right policy to diversify sources of coal to emerging black mining companies and this coal mining companies became almost a flagship for black economic empowerment in South Africa, a very successful one.

SUPER@ CHRIS YELLAND: ENERGY EXPERT
“Now we are talking about lots of smaller mines scattered all over the place…you are now sourcing coal from numerous little coal mines.”

VO
The power stations were developed to burn a specific grade of coal. If they are fed a different grade, power cuts can result. Eskom has standing contractual agreements with many coal suppliers. And, since the price of coal has increased every year since 2003, they’re continuing to make money. But De Ruyter says, Eskom has a plan to take back control over coal quality.

SUPER@ANDRÈ DE RUYTER: CEO, ESKOM
We are also in the process of establishing an inland coal terminal. Now this inland coal terminal will be used to collect coal from a variety of junior miners, and I have to stress, it is very important for us to enable junior miners to play a key role in supplying Eskom with coal.

LINK
While studies are being done to decide on the right location for this control depot, all South Africans really want to know is, will De Ruyter be able to one day guarantee a South Africa without power cuts.

MASA: Are we going to have a dark Christmas?

SUPER@ANDRÈ DE RUYTER: CEO, ESKOM
We anticipate that Christmas when the demand is very low will be a period during which the risk of loadshedding is going to be minimal. So at this point in time, we don’t anticipate that there will be any loadshedding during the December period.

MASA: Can we take your word for that?

SUPER@ANDRÈ DE RUYTER: CEO, ESKOM
“That is why Eskom keeps me very humble. You make forecasts and predictions about loadshedding at your peril as I have learned. That is why there will always be a residual risk considering our reserve margin being so low. And we are doing a lot to improve.

VO
The lights CAME on just in time for local elections to run smoothly. But South Africans WILL have to wait and see WHAT HAPPENS after election posters are taken down.


PROMOS

PROMO 1 11”
Eskom has become a liability for the economy. While it is relying so heavily on South Africans to save the utility from collapsing, its power cuts are a threat to the collapse of the entire economy.


PROMO 2 21”
It has been fourteen years since South Africans were introduced to loadshedding. And Eskom is still dishing out the same excuses every time the lights go out.

UPSOUND ADR -- “Bear in mind that recovering from neglected maintenance is a very tough job to do.”

What is the utility really doing to fix the broken mess it has become? (ADD 3 SECONDS)


PROMO 3 21”
An economy cannot grow if it doesn’t have electricity. Eskom’s constant power cuts are chasing potential investors away. Why is South African at the mercy of an embattled utility and is there any hope of change on the horizon?

UPSOUND MIKE SCHUSSLER -- “People don’t want to invest in countries where there is no power… and our own business and consumers lose confidence.”
